name: AI Deep Dive — PUMP — 2026-05-02
rationale: ProPetro Holding is a hydraulic fracturing company in structural decline. Revenue down 24.7% YoY, margins near zero (0.06% TTM), and analyst EPS consensus is NEGATIVE for Y1 (-$0.155) with barely-positive Y2 ($0.296). The analyst mean price target of $15.45 is BELOW the current price of $16.62. Piotroski 4/9. The raw data contained a share count error (shares_diluted 82.4M < shares_outstanding 122.6M — corrected to 122.7M mktcap-implied). Weighted DCF fair value $4.92 vs $16.62 = SELL (-70.4%).

bear.rationale: E&P capex cuts accelerate. Revenue declines 5% CAGR from $1.27B base ($982M by Y5). Margin barely positive at 1% as SG&A and fixed costs cannot be cut proportionally with revenue decline. Historical precedent: PUMP's FY2023 had -9.6% margin (lost $138M). Significant stock dilution as company issues shares to fund operations/acquisitions (+5%/yr). Exit PE 6x on minimal earnings. The combination of revenue decline + near-zero margins + dilution = catastrophic value destruction. PV $0.19.

base.rationale: Analyst revenue recovery: Y1 $1.22B (-3.9%), Y2 $1.43B (+17.3%). Base 5% CAGR from $1.27B = $1.62B by Y5, consistent with Y2 analyst estimate. Net margin 4% = modest recovery from 0.06% TTM. Exit PE 12x = oilfield services median for a low-margin provider. QM 0.90 (no durable moat — commodity service). Year 5: $1,619.8M × 4% / 122.6M shares = $0.53 EPS × 12 × 0.90 / 1.61 = $3.54. Note: analyst Y2 EPS $0.30 implies only 2.6% margin at $1.43B revenue — our base 4% at Y5 may be slightly optimistic.

bull.rationale: Catalyst: Oil price recovery to $90+ AND ProPetro successfully integrates its recent acquisitions to gain Permian Basin scale advantage. Revenue grows 12% CAGR to $2.24B by Y5. Margin recovers to 8% (FY2022 peak was 5.25%). Exit PE 18x. Bull PV $17.15 — essentially equal to current $16.62, illustrating that even the optimistic scenario barely justifies current price.

aiThesis.rationale: ProPetro Holding is a hydraulic fracturing company with near-zero margins, declining revenue, and an analyst price target BELOW the current trading price. The stock at $16.62 trades above the analyst consensus target of $15.45 — a rare and bearish signal. Revenue has declined 24.7% year-over-year. TTM net margin is 0.06% — essentially breakeven. The company is projected to be UNPROFITABLE in FY2026 (analyst EPS -$0.155) before barely recovering to $0.30 EPS in FY2027. A key data quality issue: the API reported shares_diluted (82.4M) below shares_outstanding (122.6M) — an impossible figure (diluted must always exceed outstanding). The DCF was recalculated with the corrected 122.6M share count, giving fair value of $4.92 vs $16.62 (-70.4%). In a commodity service industry with no durable competitive advantage, paying any significant P/E multiple for a company with negative forward earnings is difficult to justify. The bull case at $17.15 (oil price recovery + acquisition synergies) is essentially equal to current price — the risk/reward is deeply asymmetric to the downside. SELL.

analyticsLog.shareCountMethod: CRITICAL DATA ERROR in API: shares_diluted = 82,400,000 < shares_outstanding = 122,616,976 — impossible (diluted shares must always be >= outstanding). Mktcap-implied: $2.038B / $16.62 = 122.6M. CORRECTED shares to 122,616,976 (= outstanding = mktcap-implied). DCF was re-run with corrected share count. Original erroneous DCF with 82.4M shares gave $7.32 FV — share-count-corrected DCF gives $4.92 FV. The $4.92 FV is the correct figure.
analyticsLog.marginAnchor: Mean-reverting with extreme volatility. Historical: 0.16% → 5.25% → -9.55% → 0.06% (TTM). 4-yr avg: -1.02% — barely above breakeven averaged. The FY2023 loss (-9.55%) is the risk anchor: when fracking pricing pressure hits, PUMP loses money. Analyst Y1 EPS -$0.155 confirms near-term losses continue. Using near-zero to low positive margins (1%/4%/8%) acknowledging the historically terrible average.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Revenue declining: $1.28B → $1.63B → $1.44B → $1.27B TTM. 24.7% decline YoY. Analyst Y1 $1.22B (-3.9%), Y2 $1.43B (+17.3%) — flat-to-recovery trajectory. Base 5% CAGR from Y2 recovery. Bear -5% = further deterioration. Bull 12% = oil price recovery + acquisition synergies.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Energy — Oil & Gas Equipment & Services: conservative P/E 6-8, median 12-18, growth 20+. PUMP's near-zero margins make P/E unreliable as a valuation anchor. Forward PE 57.6x on $0.29 EPS (Y2) = still expensive on normalized earnings.
dataQualityFlags: CRITICAL: API shares_diluted (82,400,000) < shares_outstanding (122,616,976) — data error. Diluted shares must be >= outstanding. Corrected to 122,616,976. All EPS calculations use 122.6M. Original erroneous DCF would have given $7.32 — corrected is $4.92.
Revenue declining 24.7% YoY — from $1.44B to $1.27B. This is not just a slowdown; it is active revenue contraction.
4-yr average net margin of -1.02% — the company is barely profitable on average. FY2023 had -$138M net loss (-9.55% margin).
Analyst target $15.45 < current $16.62 — the stock is trading ABOVE analyst target. 'Buy' rating with below-target price is contradictory; likely a stale rating.
Analyst Y1 EPS -$0.155 means the company is expected to be UNPROFITABLE in the next fiscal year. Any company trading at a positive P/E with negative forward EPS is in a precarious valuation position.
